- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.10) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.20), model often overpredicts; reduce forecast to reflect bearish pressure.  
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 days); apply a 1-2 day lag correction to avoid overreaction.  
- Mean reversion bias: if 3-5 consecutive days show downward trend, model may hold too low; adjust upward by 0.5–1.5% to capture rebound.  
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates true price peaks in late period (last 7–10 days); add 0.5–1.5% buffer to final 5–7 days of forecast.  
- If sentiment swings sharply (e.g., +0.30 to -0.30 in 2–3 days), model fails to adjust; apply a 1–2 day smoothing filter to avoid erratic corrections.
